source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

china_plus_one.evidence: Company markets itself around India's 'tech self-reliance' and 'Make in India' servers built on AMD platforms; CEO stated 'this range of servers represents our commitment to the Make in India mission and highlights our capabilities to produce world-class technology indigenously.' This is framed as import-substitution/domestic manufacturing rather than an explicit export-oriented China+1 narrative; exports are a small (~9%) share of revenue.

govt_capex.evidence: Company investor presentation states government customers represent 42.8% of revenue vs 57.2% non-government; holds verified Class-I Local Supplier status under PPP-MII, making it eligible for central government/PSU/defence server tenders above Rs 50 crore where Dell, HPE, Lenovo do not qualify. Addressable government/PSU/defence server market estimated at Rs 6,000-8,000 crore annually.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports were ~9% of revenue in Q3 FY25, implying limited overall foreign-currency revenue exposure; no specific hedging policy disclosure found in available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: Received incentive of Rs 5.93 crore under PLI Scheme 2.0 for IT Hardware for the period July 2023-March 2024 (an earlier claim of similar magnitude was also disclosed); company is a confirmed IT Hardware PLI 2.0 beneficiary, though the incentive amount is a small fraction (<1%) of FY25 revenue of ~Rs 1,149 crore.

china_plus_one.evidence: ABB has invested >US$230m over the past decade in India manufacturing, including a US$75m investment across five locations for data centers, renewable energy, and metro rail; press coverage frames India's rise as a manufacturing hub amid global supply-chain rebalancing away from China, though ABB's own reporting emphasizes a 'local for local' strategy rather than explicit China+1 language tied directly to revenue growth. Q4 2024 revenue growth was partly attributed to 'growth in export markets' within the Distribution Solutions division.

govt_capex.evidence: Revenue growth in 2024 was linked to data center orders (EPC customers), and railways/metro segments saw 'significant traction,' implying some government/infrastructure-linked demand, but no quantified % of revenue from government/infra capex was found in available sources.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export markets (via Distribution Solutions/Electrification) were cited as a growth driver in 2024 but no quantified USD/export revenue % or hedging policy was found.

pli_scheme.evidence: No dedicated PLI scheme exists for heavy electrical equipment/industrial automation (ABB India's core segments); no evidence found of ABB India participating in any PLI scheme.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company messaging describes its 'geographically diversified revenue base' (sales across 70+ countries spanning Europe, Canada, and Emerging Markets) as 'a strategic strength, reducing dependency on a single market' — this is framed as revenue-market diversification, not an explicit China+1 supply-chain/API-sourcing narrative. FY25 international revenue grew 22.1%, with Rest of World +42%, Canada +16%, Europe +13%.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Natural hedge: offsets foreign currency payables (trade obligations, loans) against foreign currency receivables; monitors currency positions and may use financial instruments or operational adjustments for residual risk.
inr_exposure.evidence: Export/international revenue (multi-currency: EUR, CAD, and Emerging Market currencies, not solely USD) was 53.7% of FY25 revenue (₹4,236 crore of ₹7,896 crore total); domestic revenue ₹3,660 crore (46.3%). Company applies a natural hedging approach rather than disclosing a formal derivative hedging % policy in sources reviewed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Emcure was approved under Group B of the Government of India's PLI Scheme for Pharmaceuticals (bulk drugs/API-linked incentive scheme); specific revenue % attributable to PLI incentives not disclosed in sources reviewed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Press coverage of Hitachi Energy's India investment (new Tamil Nadu manufacturing/tech expansion, ~Rs 1,000 crore pledged; new High Voltage Products factories in Bangalore/Chennai) explicitly frames India as being used 'as a China Plus One manufacturing base for sophisticated electrical components,' with the company 'mitigating global supply chain risks while capturing domestic demand' from India's 500 GW renewable energy target by 2030 and shifting toward high-value technology exports and GCC functions.

govt_capex.evidence: Order book heavily linked to government/PSU transmission capex: won HVDC transmission orders (Khavda-Nagpur, Bhadla-Fatehpur) in consortium with BHEL, and a bulk order from POWERGRID for 30 units of 765kV/500MVA transformers. India's inter-state transmission capex plan (~Rs 3.4 trillion over six years) is a key demand driver cited for the sector; order backlog reported around Rs 29,500 crore (up 53% YoY) per broker notes, though the AR itself was not directly read to confirm an exact revenue % from government/PSU customers.

crude_exposure.evidence: Broker commentary cites 'metal inflation' (copper/steel, transformer inputs) as a margin risk factor, not crude-oil-linked raw materials, so left null.

inr_exposure.evidence: One source estimated export contribution 'expected to remain in the 25-30% range' with exports mainly to SAARC/Southeast Asia; a Q4FY26 unrealized FX loss of ₹31.5 crore was cited as a risk factor, indicating meaningful unhedged foreign-currency exposure, but no formal hedging policy percentage was found in sources reviewed.

pli_scheme.evidence: No PLI scheme exists for grid/transformer/heavy electrical equipment manufacturing; no evidence of Hitachi Energy India PLI participation found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Consolidated FY25 revenue split: India Rs 10,610.15 cr, Outside India Rs 847.33 cr (~7.4% of total Rs 11,457.48 cr) — Note 52 Segment Information. Standalone BRSR discloses export contribution to turnover of just 0.30%. No China+1 or supply-chain-diversification narrative appears anywhere in the MD&A.

rural.evidence: MD&A: 'the rural segment showed signs of recovery, supported by improved agricultural output and rising [incomes]' — no quantified revenue share given. BRSR wage-cost-by-location (not revenue) table: Rural 10.32%, Semi-urban 4.17%, Urban 30.44%, Metropolitan 55.07% (FY25).

govt_capex.evidence: MD&A references government's infrastructure-development thrust and 'Make in India' benefiting the protective/industrial coatings segment, while elsewhere noting subdued government infrastructure spending as a demand headwind during the year; no quantified % of revenue tied to govt capex disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Standalone financial risk note: 'The Company does not have any significant variable rate interest bearing liabilities as at March 31, 2025 and March 31, 2024, hence there would not be any material impact on pretax profit...' — floating-rate debt exposure is minimal/immaterial.

crude_exposure.evidence: AR discusses use of resins/monomers (crude derivatives) in paint manufacturing and references commodity price risk management, but does not disclose a quantified % of raw material cost linked to crude oil. Risk note: 'The Company doesn't enter into any long term contract with its suppliers for hedging its commodity price risk.'

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company/Group uses forward currency contracts to hedge foreign exchange risk on a short-term basis 'when commercially expedient'; standalone foreign exchange earnings (Rs 3.17 cr) vs outgo (Rs 1,195.75 cr) show FX outgo (imports) far exceeds FX earnings.
inr_exposure.evidence: Outside-India revenue (~7.4% of consolidated) spans multiple foreign subsidiaries (incl. Bolix in Poland, Nepal, Russia operations), so is not purely USD-denominated.

pli_scheme.evidence: No mention of PLI scheme participation anywhere in the FY25 Integrated Annual Report; paints/coatings is not among India's PLI-covered sectors.

china_plus_one.evidence: No management commentary frames Eicher's export growth as a China+1 diversification story. Instead, recent coverage highlights a China dependency risk: 'Royal Enfield maker adapts to China's export curbs' on rare-earth magnets, which affected production of Himalayan/Scram/Guerrilla models (2025).

rural.evidence: Management commentary around FY25 results: rural demand is rising and continuing to outpace urban sales growth for Royal Enfield, with tier-2/tier-3 town penetration seen as a growth driver; no quantified rural revenue share disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Eicher carries a light balance sheet (~Rs 3.8 billion total debt per market data, largely net-cash); no specific floating-rate debt disclosure found in sources reviewed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Earnings-call commentary (Q1 FY26): input cost increases across aluminum, crude oil, steel, copper and precious metals had a ~4-4.5% net impact on costs in a recent quarter, partly offset (~0.4%) via value-engineering/cost programs. No AR-disclosed % of raw material cost specifically linked to crude oil found.

inr_exposure.evidence: International/export business revenue was ~Rs 2,546 crore (+38% YoY) in FY25, ~13.5% of consolidated revenue of ~Rs 18,870 crore. Revenue is spread across multiple currencies (USD, GBP, EUR, BRL, ARS, etc.) via CKD assembly units in Argentina, Colombia, Thailand, Brazil, Bangladesh and Nepal — not purely USD-denominated. No specific hedging-policy disclosure located.

pli_scheme.evidence: Unconfirmed — one non-primary source speculated Eicher could benefit from India's Auto PLI scheme (potential incentives cited, unverified) tied to EV/localization investment, but this could not be corroborated against Eicher's actual annual report or official disclosures within available fetches.

china_plus_one.evidence: No explicit China+1 / supply-chain-diversification narrative found; Coforge is an IT-services exporter (not manufacturing), so this signal does not directly apply. Company messaging instead emphasizes vendor consolidation, GCC-to-GVC transformation for clients, and reduced client-concentration risk (top-10 client revenue share declining).

rate_sensitive.evidence: Coforge has taken on acquisition financing (e.g., for the ~$2.5bn Cigniti Technologies acquisition and other bolt-ons) and carries rated bank loan facilities (CRISIL), implying some debt exposure, but no specific floating-rate-liability percentage was found in sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Coforge designates foreign-currency forward contracts as cash-flow hedges for its foreign-currency (USD/GBP/EUR) revenue exposure; the effective portion of fair-value changes is routed through the Cash Flow Hedging Reserve and reclassified to P&L (Revenue) when the hedged transaction affects profit or loss (Ind AS 109-based disclosure).
inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 revenue by client geography: Americas ~53.9%, EMEA ~34.7% (predominantly non-INR, largely USD/GBP/EUR revenue). FY25 total revenue was US$1,468 million (~Rs 12,215 crore), up 32% YoY in constant currency — consistent with an overwhelmingly export/foreign-currency revenue base typical of Indian IT services exporters.

pli_scheme.evidence: PLI scheme is not applicable to the IT services sector; no mention found in sources reviewed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Radico is a domestic-focused IMFL/spirits company with exports contributing an estimated ~8-9% of revenue (and ~4-5% of volume) across ~85 countries; no China+1 or supply-chain-diversification narrative found in sources reviewed.

rural.evidence: No explicit rural/semi-urban revenue split found in sources reviewed; company narrative emphasizes premiumisation (Prestige & Above portfolio, ~69.4% of IMFL value in FY25) and international expansion rather than rural-specific exposure.

rate_sensitive.evidence: As of Sep 2024, Radico had ~Rs 815 crore gross debt (~Rs 744 crore net debt) with EBIT covering interest ~6.9x; the specific floating- vs fixed-rate debt split was not disclosed in sources reviewed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key raw-material cost pressure in FY25 came from grain/ENA (extra neutral alcohol) and glass — foodgrain inflation had a ~335 bps negative impact on gross margin in Q1 FY25; more recent commentary flags 15-20% glass-bottle price inflation. These inputs are primarily agri-commodity and packaging-glass linked rather than directly crude-oil-linked; no explicit crude-oil-linked raw-material % was disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports reach ~85 countries and are estimated to contribute ~8-9% of revenue; export and non-IMFL segment revenue was expected to cross Rs 500 crore net sales in FY26. No specific USD hedging-policy disclosure found in sources reviewed.

pli_scheme.evidence: No PLI scheme participation found; alcoholic beverages are not covered under India's PLI scheme list.

china_plus_one.evidence: Honasa is a predominantly domestic D2C beauty/personal-care company (Mamaearth, The Derma Co, Aqualogica, BBlunt, Dr. Sheth's); reports describe 'selective exports and marketplace listings' as a small, expanding contributor, but no China+1/supply-chain-diversification narrative was found.

rural.evidence: Company cites deepening penetration into 'urban and semi-urban markets' and offline expansion to 270,000+ outlets (5-yr revenue CAGR ~46%), but no explicit rural revenue percentage was found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Packaging (PE/PP/PET resins) used in personal-care products is crude-oil price linked; industry commentary (covering HUL, Honasa/Mamaearth, etc.) flags exposure to crude/palm-oil-linked packaging cost inflation amid 2026 Middle East crude spikes, but Honasa itself has not disclosed a specific % and declined comment citing a 'silent period.'

inr_exposure.evidence: Revenue is overwhelmingly INR-denominated given >95% domestic manufacturing/sales; some raw materials/intermediates are sourced via Gulf-region supply chains, creating indirect forex/input-cost exposure. No explicit hedging policy found.

pli_scheme.evidence: No PLI scheme applicable to personal-care/D2C FMCG business was found referenced for Honasa.

china_plus_one.evidence: HAL's FY25 revenue mix was ~23% manufacturing + ~70% repair/overhaul (both domestic, ~93% combined), with exports plus design & development together only ~7%. Growth narrative centers on domestic indigenization/Atmanirbhar Bharat (Tejas Mk1A, Su-30 upgrade, LUH, Dornier-25) driven by Indian MoD orders, not a China+1 export-diversification story.

govt_capex.evidence: HAL is a defence PSU whose customers are overwhelmingly the Indian Ministry of Defence/armed forces; ~93% of revenue is domestic (manufacturing + repair/overhaul). Order book rose to ~₹2,58,942 crore (Sep 2025) from ~₹1,33,238 crore (Dec 2024), driven by government indigenization programs; company also guided a 5-year capex plan of ₹14,000-15,000 crore tied to capacity expansion for government defence programs.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports (~7% of revenue) are the primary foreign-currency revenue source; majority of revenue is INR-denominated domestic government contracts. Foreign-currency exposure also arises from imported aircraft/engine components. Specific hedging policy not found.

pli_scheme.evidence: No dedicated PLI scheme identified covering HAL; its growth is linked to indigenization/Atmanirbhar Bharat defence-procurement policy rather than a PLI framework.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company commentary notes it has 'gained from a trend in which pharmaceutical corporations shift some production to India rather than China,' and its CDMO business (rebranded 'Navin Molecular') is positioned to let customers 'build a geographically diverse supply chain.' More than 40% of products are exported to North America, Europe, Middle East and Asia Pacific, with CDMO orders reported from EU and US majors. Framing is diversification/export-momentum rather than an explicit repeated 'China+1' label, hence rated moderate rather than strong.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key raw materials are fluorspar (imported; ~60% of global supply from just 3 countries) and other basic/chlorinated chemicals; company took a 25% stake in a fluorspar-beneficiation JV for backward integration. Some intermediates are petrochemical-derived, but no explicit crude-oil-linked raw-material percentage was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: More than 40% of revenue comes from exports (North America, Europe, Middle East, Asia Pacific), implying meaningful USD/foreign-currency revenue exposure; specific hedging policy not found.

pli_scheme.evidence: No confirmed PLI scheme participation found for Navin Fluorine despite ongoing India fluoropolymer/chemicals PLI discussions; not verified in sources reviewed.

china_plus_one.evidence: EIL is an engineering consultancy/EPC PSU serving primarily Indian and Middle East oil & gas/petrochemical clients (e.g., ADNOC in Abu Dhabi); no China+1 supply-chain-diversification narrative was found.

govt_capex.evidence: EIL is a Government of India PSU (GoI holds 51.32% equity) under the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas; its business is described as heavily tied to 'the government's capex push in the oil and gas sector,' with consultancy for major PSU clients (ONGC, IOCL, BPCL, HPCL, etc.) and having engineered 11 of the 12 mega petrochemical complexes in India. No precise revenue percentage from government/PSU clients was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: EIL has a growing overseas consultancy business, particularly in the Middle East (revenue from that region reportedly grew from ~₹30 crore to ~₹1,000 crore over 3-4 years via an Abu Dhabi engineering hub serving ADNOC and others), implying rising foreign-currency (USD-linked) revenue exposure, but no explicit % of total revenue or hedging policy was found.

pli_scheme.evidence: EIL provides engineering/consultancy services (including green hydrogen and petrochemical project design) to clients in PLI-eligible sectors (chemicals/petrochemicals PLI, SIGHT green-hydrogen program), but EIL itself was not confirmed as a direct PLI scheme beneficiary in sources reviewed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Exports are minimal (~6% of revenue, reportedly ~20% of volumes). Growth narrative in available sources is domestic infrastructure/urbanization-led (PMAY, Jal Jeevan Mission water-tank tenders), not China+1 driven. No China+1 framing found.

rural.evidence: Company cites government push into semi-urban/rural infrastructure (e.g., Jal Jeevan Mission elevated water tank tenders) as a demand driver via its ~800-distributor, 300+ town network, but no specific rural revenue % disclosed in sources reviewed.

govt_capex.evidence: MD&A-adjacent commentary cites government infrastructure spend (Jal Jeevan Mission, PMAY, roads) as a structural demand driver for structural steel tubes (e.g., a cited UP government tender for 60,000 water tanks implying ~1 million MT tube opportunity). No explicit % of revenue from government capex disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company is described as low-leverage; a planned ~₹500 crore capex over 2-3 years is stated to be funded entirely through internal accruals, implying minimal reliance on debt.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports account for only ~6% of revenue; business is overwhelmingly domestic and INR-denominated.

pli_scheme.evidence: Not found among the ~30 companies/67 approved projects under India's PLI Scheme for Specialty Steel (list dominated by primary steel producers - Tata Steel, JSW Steel, JSPL, AMNS India, SAIL, Shyam Metalics, etc.); APL Apollo is a downstream structural-tube/pipe manufacturer, not a primary specialty-steel producer covered by that scheme.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company commentary discusses reducing dependence on Chinese-sourced APIs/intermediates (reportedly from ~46% toward a ~35% target) as a supply-chain risk-mitigation measure for its own manufacturing inputs, rather than framing China+1 as driving export/order growth from customers diversifying away from China. Does not match the customer-driven China+1 pattern seen in CDMO/API-export peers.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company commentary indicates use of natural hedges (USD-denominated receivables offsetting payables) plus forward contracts to manage FX volatility on export revenue; no specific hedge-ratio was verifiable from a primary source in this session.
inr_exposure.evidence: US Formulations (~47% of consolidated revenue) plus International Markets Formulations (~9%) form the bulk of foreign-currency revenue; US business alone is guided to a ~US$1bn run-rate.

pli_scheme.evidence: Company is expanding domestic API capacity (including a pending Sterling Biotech API business acquisition) and reducing China-sourcing dependence, consistent with the government's Bulk Drug PLI/self-reliance push, but explicit confirmation that Zydus Lifesciences is a formally approved beneficiary under the PLI Scheme for Bulk Drugs was not found in sources reviewed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Divi's is consistently characterized in company/analyst commentary as a primary beneficiary of the 'China+1' strategy in CDMO/custom synthesis, with capacity expansion (new Kakinada Unit-III, commercial operations from Jan 2025) linked to global innovator and generic customers diversifying API/CRAMS sourcing away from China. Custom synthesis (~56% of product mix) is cited as the key growth driver, with incremental order wins and client additions attributed to this diversification trend and an approx. US$20bn molecules-going-off-patent opportunity.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Divi's is generally characterized as a low-debt, cash-generative company; no specific floating-rate liability disclosure was found in sources reviewed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Divi's APIs/intermediates rely substantially on petrochemical-derived feedstocks, with imports reported to account for roughly 45% of raw material consumption per analyst commentary, implying indirect crude-oil-linked cost exposure. No specific % of raw material cost tied to crude/petrochemical pricing was verifiable from a primary source.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Exports (predominantly USD/EUR-denominated) are reported to be managed via forward contracts per general industry/analyst commentary; specific hedge-ratio or policy wording could not be verified from the AR directly in this session (company site access blocked).
inr_exposure.evidence: Exports comprise ~88-90% of sales, with Europe and the US together contributing roughly 72-74% of revenue.

pli_scheme.evidence: Divi's Laboratories was not found in the Department of Pharmaceuticals' published list of approved applicants under the PLI Scheme for Bulk Drugs; growth is attributed in sources to China+1/CDMO demand and organic capacity expansion (Kakinada Units III/IV) rather than PLI incentives.

china_plus_one.evidence: Purely domestic financial-products distribution/wealth-management business (mutual funds, PMS, AIFs) serving Indian clients; no export/manufacturing exposure, so a China+1 narrative is not applicable.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Anand Rathi Wealth's listed distribution business is reported as almost debt-free (debt-to-equity ~2.4%). However, group NBFC affiliate Anand Rathi Global Finance Ltd (ARGFL), which funds the structured-products business (~28-29% of AUM), carries on-book gearing of roughly 11.5x, with borrowings largely via market-linked debentures — a more relevant rate-sensitive exposure than the listed entity's own balance sheet, though not directly consolidated floating-rate liability disclosure.

inr_exposure.evidence: No meaningful foreign-currency revenue; business is domestic wealth/financial-products distribution.

pli_scheme.evidence: Financial-services distribution business; PLI (manufacturing-linked) schemes are not applicable to this sector.

china_plus_one.evidence: Astral's UK subsidiary Seal IT Services exports adhesives/sealants throughout Europe, Africa and the Middle East, and overall exports are estimated at roughly 8% of consolidated revenue. No explicit China+1 / supply-chain-diversification framing was found in the sources available.

rural.evidence: Astral's plumbing pipes business is a cited beneficiary of rural water-infrastructure programs (Jal Jeevan Mission, outlay extended to ~₹8.7 lakh crore covering rural tap-water connections), per analyst/press commentary, but no specific rural revenue % was disclosed in sources found.

govt_capex.evidence: Analyst and press commentary (e.g. on Jal Jeevan Mission extension) repeatedly names Astral among pipe-sector beneficiaries of government rural/urban water-infrastructure capex, but no specific % of company revenue tied to government contracts was found.

crude_exposure.evidence: PVC resin, Astral's primary raw material for plumbing pipes, is a crude-oil/naphtha-linked petrochemical feedstock (ethylene-based PVC production cost is tied to crude oil prices per industry commentary); FY25 PBILDT margin was ~16.34% (PY 16.52%) amid raw-material volatility, but no specific raw-material-cost % was disclosed in sources found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Given exports are estimated at only ~8% of revenue, direct USD revenue exposure appears limited; no specific hedging policy disclosure was found in sources available.

pli_scheme.evidence: No evidence found of Astral participating in any PLI scheme; plastic pipes/adhesives is not a PLI-covered category.

china_plus_one.evidence: FY2024-25 results commentary notes Bosch Limited's Powertrain Solutions division grew sales 5.8%, driven by the tractor segment and 'an increase in export sales'; Mobility business overall product sales rose 7.0% with domestic sales up 6.2%. No explicit China+1 / supply-chain-diversification framing was found in available sources; revenue is largely domestic (India) with exports a secondary driver.

rural.evidence: Tractor-segment growth (rural-linked demand) was cited as a driver of Powertrain Solutions sales in FY25, but no specific rural revenue % was disclosed in sources found.

crude_exposure.evidence: No specific crude-oil-linked raw material % was disclosed in sources found; Bosch India's inputs are primarily metal/electronic components rather than petrochemicals.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 revenue reported as ~INR 18,087 crore (~EUR 1,985 million) alongside parent Robert Bosch GmbH's EUR reporting, implying some FX translation exposure, but no specific USD/FX revenue % or hedging policy was found in sources available.

pli_scheme.evidence: Third-party/secondary industry summaries list Bosch among companies associated with India's PLI scheme for Automobile and Auto Components (Component Champion Incentive Scheme), alongside Maruti Suzuki, Hero MotoCorp, Motherson Sumi, Lucas-TVS etc. This could not be confirmed against Bosch Limited's own annual report MD&A, so it is treated as unconfirmed.

china_plus_one.evidence: B2B segment export underlying volume growth was 18% in Q1 FY25 (vs domestic), and separate press commentary notes Pidilite 'expects export rebound after tariff cut, eyes double-digit growth,' implying tariff-driven export softness followed by recovery. No explicit China+1 / supply-chain-diversification narrative was found; exports remain a small (~8%) share of revenue.

rural.evidence: Pidilite's Consumer & Bazaar segment (~79-80% of consolidated revenue) relies on a deep distribution network historically covering 4,000+ distributors and 400,000+ retailers, explicitly reaching semi-urban and rural markets less accessible to global competitors; no specific rural revenue % was disclosed in sources found.

govt_capex.evidence: Pidilite's B2B 'Large Users Business' (construction/engineering chemicals) hosted an FY25 event ('Engineers' Edge: Beyond Blueprints') with major infrastructure/EPC players including Tata Projects, L&T and Reliance Industries, indicating some infra-adjacent B2B demand, but no % of revenue tied to government capex specifically was disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Vinyl acetate monomer (VAM), a crude-oil derivative, accounts for approximately 35-40% of Pidilite's raw material costs per analyst/press commentary; normalization of VAM prices was cited as a margin tailwind for FY25 (consolidated revenue ~₹13,400 crore, EBITDA CAGR ~17%).

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports were cited at roughly ₹993 crore against total revenue in the ₹13,400-14,600 crore range (under 10% of revenue); the company also imports crude-linked feedstocks like VAM, implying USD-denominated cost exposure on the input side. No specific formal hedging policy disclosure was found in sources available.

pli_scheme.evidence: No evidence found of Pidilite participating in any PLI scheme; adhesives/specialty chemicals for consumer and B2B markets is not a PLI-covered category for this company.

china_plus_one.evidence: Sona Comstar is described as India's largest importer of rare-earth magnets and announced plans for local rare-earth-magnet production explicitly in response to mainland China's export restrictions, directly de-risking a critical EV-driveline input from China. The company (12 manufacturing/assembly facilities across India, USA, Mexico and China) derives over 50% of sales from international markets and is a leading BEV differential-assembly supplier in North America and a top player in Europe, consistent with global OEMs sourcing EV driveline content outside China. Company commentary also frames its FY25 China market entry (via a Beijing JV) as reinforcing a 'China+1' strategy in reverse -- selectively partnering in China while diversifying its own supply base and end-markets across North America, Europe and Asia.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company's long-term debt was reported as very low (~₹80 million in FY25 vs ~₹292 million in FY24, a ~73% decline), suggesting limited leverage/floating-rate liability exposure overall, but no specific floating-rate % or debt-mix disclosure was found in sources available.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 geography split cited: India ~29%, North America ~41%, Europe ~24% (implied), rest of Asia ~6% of ~₹3,555 crore revenue -- i.e. roughly 65-70% of revenue is North America + Europe (largely USD/EUR-denominated), consistent with the company's own description of deriving 'over 50% of sales' from international markets. No specific hedging policy disclosure was found in sources available.

pli_scheme.evidence: Sona Comstar became the first Indian auto-component supplier to receive PLI certification under the Ministry of Heavy Industries' Auto PLI (Advanced Automotive Technology) scheme, specifically for its hub-wheel-drive motor for electric two-wheelers (developed in-house, launched 2020); the company had filed seven applications for different products under the scheme. Specific revenue contribution from PLI-linked products was not disclosed in sources found.
